you'd freeze at the edge.

captions.text: Friends far away would watch you slow down.
Then stop, just short of the edge.

beats.vo: Friends far away would watch you slow down. Then stop, just short of the edge.

captions.text: That edge is the event horizon.
Point of no return.
Not even light escapes.

beats.vo: That edge is the event horizon. Point of no return. Not even light escapes.

captions.text: Why?
Gravity bends space and time so hard,
your picture slows to a stop.

beats.vo: Why? Gravity bends space and time so hard, your picture slows to a stop.

captions.text: On your own clock, NASA's simulation says,
the fall takes about three hours.

captions.text: A giant black hole, about four million Suns.
Like the one in our galaxy's center.

captions.text: Cross the edge,
and space itself rushes inward at light speed.

twelve point eight seconds,
before you're torn apart.

You stretch like a noodle.

captions.text: Scientists really call it spaghettification.
A small black hole is worse.
It can tear you apart before the edge.

captions.text: At the center,
math says a point of endless crush.
Nobody knows if it's real.

This is math, not a memory.
